3. `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/README.md` — its "Working discipline" section is binding on you: **change the simulator first**, let the red tests name the scenarios the change breaks, then move prose and tests together.
4. `docs/tasks-dispatch/SCENARIOS.md` (read §H and §I; earlier sections are superseded record).
5. The engine: `engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `executor.mjs`, `work-item.mjs`, `anchors.mjs`, `signals.mjs`, and `engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs`.

Today a scheduled task's occurrence costs a GitHub issue whether or not there is work, and a declined occurrence *rolls* — leaving a permanently-open `task:blocked` issue saying "next window at X". Only tasks whose anchor has come and whose occurrence is not already covered get evaluated — never the whole task list every hour.

**B. Fail-open, everywhere.** If signals cannot be collected for a task (a missing credential — the scheduler stub carries no `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, unlike the executor workflow), create the item exactly as today and let the executor decide. Never fewer runs because a read failed. Same for an unreadable/absent board: treat as absent, evaluate. A precondition that throws is fail-open too.

   - It is the watermark: "have I already asked this task about this anchor?". A row whose last-asked equals the current anchor means do not re-ask this occurrence.
   - **Rewrite only when a row actually changes.** A run that changes nothing writes nothing — this is also the standing tidy-repo "record changes, never scans" rule.
   - Parse/serialize of the board lives in exactly one module, the way `work-item.mjs` owns the work item's schema. A malformed or partially-parsable board degrades to "absent" per-row, never throws.
   - Budget the body two-tier against the ~64KB field cap even though it is trivial at ~25 rows.
   - It must be created lazily — only when there is a first row to write.

Keep `Not-before` itself — it is still the blocked-item / request / first-ever-item mechanism; only the *roll* goes. Check every reader of the roll (the janitor's sleeping-item rule, `isReleasable`, the dashboard, the sim) and move them with it.

**E. One-time migration.** The first run that understands the new shape closes today's sleeping standing items (open, `task:blocked`, a `Not-before` in the future, no `Blocked-by`) with a comment saying why, and seeds their rows onto the board.    - `engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs:177` excludes `/^\[claudinite-(task|work)\]/` from the `issues` collector. `[claudinite-schedule]` passes straight through, so every board rewrite would land in `issues.touched` and wake `tidy-issues`.    - The board must not be picked up by `planSchedulerRun`'s title-exact work-item family match, nor by `listOpenWorkItems`, nor by the janitor. Distinct prefix, distinct fetch path — verify each reader.
   - The executor still re-evaluates at pick, unchanged. The board's verdict is a watermark, never a verdict carried forward to a run.
   - Grep for every other place that filters or ignores `[claudinite-work]` / `[claudinite-task]` titles (dashboards, tidy tasks, checks, fleet code) and decide, per site, whether the new prefix belongs there too.

- Write the two-root mount form for any path/regex against the mount (`.claudinite/(shared|local)/` prefix optional).
- Comments carry the *why* and cross-file relationships, never a narration of the edit you just made.
- One concern per commit where the concerns genuinely stand alone.

## Deliverable

Work on the branch `claude/scheduler-github-noise-4ucaei` (it exists locally and on origin; base it on current `origin/main` — rebase, never merge). Commit with `Refs #1115`. Push with `git push -u origin claude/scheduler-github-noise-4ucaei`, then open a pull request (ready for review, not draft) against `main`, following any PR template in `.github/`. End every GitHub comment/PR body with a blank line, `---`, and `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_`.

Do NOT merge anything. Do NOT force a fleet delivery. Do not push to any other branch.

Return, as your final message: the PR number and URL, a per-folder summary of what changed (non-test folders only, one line each), the list of new SCENARIOS.md sections and their test names, any finding the simulator turned up, and anything you deliberately left undone with the reason.

{"number":1115,"title":"No work, no item — the scheduler run decides at the anchor and files an issue only when there is work","body":"## The problem

The queue's issues are half machine bookkeeping. Right now **12 of 46 open issues** are `[claudinite-work]` items, most of them permanently asleep — `#1040`, `#1038`, `#1037`, `#1036`, `#1034`, `#1033`, `#937` — each one saying nothing but "next window at X". On top of that the create/close cycle burns **~6.4 new issue numbers a day** (23 work items closed in the 3.6 days to 2026-08-20).

Two mechanics produce it:

- **Sleeping items never close.** When a precondition declines, `noGoPlan` (`engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs:136`) *rolls* the standing item — stamps `Not-before: `, flips it back to `task:blocked`, leaves it open. A task that never has work owns an open issue forever, and the count grows with every task adopted.
- **The item must exist before the verdict.** `planSchedulerRun` job 1 instantiates at the anchor knowing nothing about whether there is work; the verdict happens later, at pick, on the executor. So every occurrence costs an issue whether or not anything needed doing — *and* a declined occurrence dispatches a whole executor session just to roll the item and stand down.

[DESIGN.md:405](docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) named this cost and accepted it — *"read it as the dashboard it is: the issue list **is** the scheduler's state"*. That justification has lapsed: `claudinite-dashboard` now **is** the dashboard, so the issue list is paying a price for a job something else already does.

## The change

**No work, no item.** The scheduler run evaluates a task's precondition when its anchor comes and creates the work item only on a yes. A no creates nothing.

- `planSchedulerRun` job 1 gains an injectable `evaluate(task)` seam, so the decision core stays pure and fixture-testable; the shell wires `collectSignalsForTask` (`engine/scheduler/queue/signals.mjs:18`) and `evaluatePrecondition`.
- **Fail-open**: where the scheduler run cannot collect a task's signals (a missing credential — the scheduler stub carries no `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` today, unlike the executor workflow), it creates the item exactly as it does now and lets the executor decide. Never fewer runs because a read failed.
- The executor still re-evaluates at pick, unchanged — a chained stage re-derives world state rather than trusting a verdict passed forward.
- `noGoPlan`'s roll for standing items collapses into a plain close with the reason; the `Not-before` roll and its open-blocked resting state go away.
- One-time migration: the currently-open sleeping standing items are closed by the first run that understands the new shape.

### Still open

How a declined occurrence is remembered, so the next hourly run doesn't re-ask — a schedule-board issue, no state at all with hourly re-evaluation, or a fourth shape. Being explored; the answer lands in this issue before implementation.

## Why it's worth it

- Open issues become *only* work that needs doing or a human. The 12 go to at most 1.
- Issue-number burn drops **below** today's rather than doubling (the alternative shape considered, closing declined occurrences, roughly doubles it).
- Declines stop dispatching executor sessions — a container saved per declined occurrence per day.

## Costs, named

- The scheduler run stops being a pure function of the clock and the issue list ([DESIGN §5](docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md)) — it collects signals. That purity was itself the deliberate deletion of the slot scheduler's watermark machinery, so the design doc's rationale needs rewriting, not just amending.
- "Asked and declined" stops being a durable issue and becomes whatever the watermark decision above lands on.
- Signal collection for an occurrence that *does* have work happens twice (scheduler run, then executor at pick). Accepted: it is the re-derive rule, and it is paid only on occurrences that do work, against a saving on every one that doesn't.

Decision recorded on [#1115](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1115#issuecomment-5357408193), and a Fable subagent is implementing it now.

**What was settled.** One permanent open `[claudinite-schedule]` board issue per repo carries the watermark — a row per scheduled task with its last-asked anchor, verdict and next window — rewritten only when a row actually changes. The scheduler run evaluates a task's precondition when its anchor comes and files a work item only on a yes; a decline becomes a board row instead of a permanently-open `task:blocked` issue. Twelve sleeping machine issues become one that a human can actually read.

**Why not the alternatives.** Re-asking hourly with no watermark is affordable on the per-repo token, but the two `fleet`-signal tasks enumerate every owned repo per evaluation (~100–130 reads, 1–2 min each) — 24× today's cost for a verdict that moves at most daily — and it fires tasks off-anchor, which silently redefines what `daily-1h`/`daily-2h` mean for the nightly `update → growth-extract → growth-dedup → growth-promote` chain. [{"id":5357408193,"body":"## Decision: the watermark is a schedule board — one open issue per repo

The "Still open" question above is settled. Owner's call, 2026-08-20: **the open board**, and the design doc, the simulator and SCENARIOS.md move with the change rather than after it.

**The mechanism.** One permanent open issue per repo, `[claudinite-schedule]`, whose body is a table — one row per scheduled task: its frequency, the anchor it was last asked at, the verdict it gave, and the next window it wakes for. The scheduler run reads it as the watermark (*have I already asked this task about this occurrence?*) and rewrites it **only when a row changes**, so a quiet day writes nothing.

**Why this and not the alternatives.**

- *No watermark at all, re-ask every hour* — affordable on the per-repo token (~4% of the 1000/hr budget), but the two `fleet`-signal tasks (`canon-curation/growth-promote`, `growth-discover-packs`) enumerate every owned repo per evaluation: ~100–130 reads and 1–2 minutes each, so hourly re-asking is ~24× today's cost for a verdict that moves at most daily. And the "win" is a bug: a task whose signal turns true at 15:00 would fire off-anchor, which quietly redefines what `daily-1h` / `daily-2h` mean for the nightly chain (`update` → `growth-extract` → `growth-dedup` → `growth-promote` are ordered against a converged mount, not against clock latency).
- *A repo variable / the Actions cache / a Project* — each needs a permission the vendored scheduler stub does not carry (`variables: write`), a 7-day eviction window, or a credential `GITHUB_TOKEN` never gets. The board needs only `issues: write`, already in the stub, so it ships through the nightly converge with no per-member action.
- *An orphan ref* — feasible (`contents: write` is there), but it adds push machinery to a run that is pure issue mechanics today, and shows a human nothing.
- *A closed board* — identical mechanics, zero visible machine issues; rejected because the record would then be readable only through `claudinite-dashboard`, an opt-in pack most members don't declare and that `engine/` cannot depend on.

The board is a **first** authority for a genuinely new fact — "asked at anchor A, declined" is written nowhere else once the roll goes away — while the next-window column is derived from the pure `anchors.mjs` functions and regenerated every run. Durability is the easy case: a lost, deleted or vandalised board reads as *absent*, which costs one redundant evaluation and nothing else — the family guard (`created_at`/`closed_at` vs. the anchor, `scheduler-run.mjs:100`) still prevents a double run. It fails toward evaluating, never toward skipping.

**Traps the implementation must clear.**

- **Self-trigger, the F8 class.** The `issues` collector excludes `/^\[claudinite-(task|work)\]/` (`engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs:177`) — `[claudinite-schedule]` walks straight through it, so every board rewrite would land in `issues.touched` and wake `tidy-issues`. The regex is extended in the same commit.
- The board must not parse as a work-item family in `planSchedulerRun`'s title-exact match — distinct prefix, distinct fetch path.
- The executor still re-evaluates at pick. The board's verdict is a watermark, never a verdict carried forward.
- The body is budgeted two-tier against the 64KB field cap, trivial as it is at ~25 rows.

1	// The work item — the queue's one durable object (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §3, §4).
2	// An issue titled `[claudinite-work] <pack>/<task> [qualifier]`, whose labels are
3	// its state, whose body's first line is the task path, and whose optional body
4	// fields (`Not-before`, `Blocked-by`, and a request's `Request` / `Model`) are the
5	// only facts it carries beyond that.
6	//
7	// PURE, and deliberately the whole schema: everything else — anchors, guards,
8	// yields, leashes, verdicts — is computed fresh at every scheduler run and pick from the
9	// engine and the declarations at HEAD (DESIGN §14). The label-and-field vocabulary
10	// here is therefore the compatibility surface across engine versions, which is why
11	// additive change is the strongly preferred shape and a rename needs a migration.
12	//
13	// Parse/serialize of those fields lives here and nowhere else (DESIGN §9).
14	//
15	// The one import, and a frozen constant at that: the pack-rename map, which this
16	// module needs to keep reading titles written before a rename (see parseWorkItemTitle).
17	import { canonicalPackId } from '../../pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs';
18	
19	// The title prefix. Disjoint from the slot mechanism's `[claudinite-task]` on
20	// purpose: the two mechanisms coexist per-repo behind `taskScheduler.dispatch`,
21	// and neither may read the other's issues (DESIGN §14, S29).
22	export const WORK_PREFIX = '[claudinite-work]';
23	
24	export const BLOCKED = 'task:blocked';
25	export const READY = 'task:ready';
26	export const URGENT = 'task:urgent';
27	export const EXECUTING = 'task:executing';
28	export const AGENT = 'task:agent';
29	export const NEEDS_HUMAN = 'needs-human';
30	
31	// @deprecated The origin marker (DESIGN §15.26). Nothing writes it and nothing
32	// branches on it: whether an item is a task's standing occurrence or an ad-hoc run
33	// is STRUCTURAL — see `isStandingItem` — so a marker that could disagree with the
34	// structure was a second authority over the same fact. Kept exported and inert
35	// because open items filed by an older engine still carry it, and a reader that
36	// choked on an unknown label would fail on exactly those.
37	export const ORIGIN_SCHEDULE = 'origin:schedule';
38	
39	// The TRIAGE SUB-LABELS. `needs-human` says an item is parked; these say what the
40	// human parked with it is expected to DO, which is the whole difference between a
41	// queue a person can skim and one they have to read. Every park wears BOTH:
42	// `needs-human` stays the single state the machine reads (every guard, sweep and
43	// dashboard already turns on it), and the sub-label is the human's routing.
44	//
45	// The four are disjoint by REMEDY, not by cause:
46	//   action   — something outside the code must change: a secret set, a scope
47	//              granted, a routine's prompt or endpoint fixed, an item re-created
48	//              with the parameter it was missing. Mechanical; no judgement.
49	//   decision — the run stopped mid-flight and what happens next is a choice:
50	//              re-queue or abandon, does the half-done work stand, was the
51	//              ceiling violation acceptable.
52	//   approval — the run SUCCEEDED and deliberately left an unmerged PR. The only
53	//              park that is not a fault; the human merges it or closes it.
54	//   failure  — the run broke: a bug, a contract-forbidden shape, a malformed or
55	//              forged item. Someone diagnoses and fixes code.
56	// `failure` is the default a park falls back to, so an unclassified park reads as
57	// "diagnose me" rather than quietly joining the mechanical lane.
58	const triage = (kind) => `task:needs-human-${kind}`;
59	export const NEEDS_HUMAN_ACTION = triage('action');
60	export const NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION = triage('decision');
61	export const NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL = triage('approval');
62	export const NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE = triage('failure');
63	export const TRIAGE_LABELS = Object.freeze([
64	  NEEDS_HUMAN_ACTION, NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION, NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL, NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE,
65	]);
66	// WHICH PARKS HOLD THE TASK'S LANE. A task's open STANDING item is the occurrence
67	// itself, so while one exists the generator files no further occurrence
68	// (`planSchedulerRun` job 1) — which for a park means the task stops being scheduled at
69	// all until a human clears it. That is right for a `failure`: filing a queue of
70	// items that will break the same way helps nobody, and the silence is the signal.
71	// It is wrong for the other three, which are a person's inbox, not a fault in the
72	// task: a PR waiting to be approved, a choice waiting to be made and a secret
73	// waiting to be set must not also stop tomorrow's run.
74	//
75	// A park wearing NO sub-label blocks, which is what makes this safe on the way in:
76	// every item parked by an engine older than the sub-labels, and every kind word a
77	// future engine invents that this one does not know, holds the lane rather than
78	// silently letting a broken task keep filing work.
79	export const isBlockingPark = (item) =>
80	  hasLabel(item, NEEDS_HUMAN)
81	  && !hasLabel(item, NEEDS_HUMAN_ACTION)
82	  && !hasLabel(item, NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION)
83	  && !hasLabel(item, NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL);
84	
85	// A kind word (from a worker's own triage marker, or a call site) to its label.
86	// Anything unrecognised is a `failure`: a worker that misspells its class has a
87	// bug, which is exactly what that lane means.
88	export const triageLabelFor = (kind) =>
89	  (TRIAGE_LABELS.includes(triage(kind)) ? triage(kind) : NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE);
90	
91	// @deprecated Nothing writes this since the approval park: a run that left an
92	// unmerged PR no longer CLOSES as delivered, it parks at
93	// `task:needs-human-approval` and waits to be merged. Kept exported, kept in
94	// `QUEUE_LABELS`, and still read everywhere it was read — closed issues carrying
95	// it are stored data, and a decoder that stopped recognising it would turn every
96	// historical delivered run into an un-outcomed one.
97	export const OUTCOME_DELIVERED = 'outcome:delivered';
98	
99	// @deprecated The pre-2026-08-19 spellings of the two terminals below. Kept
100	// exported so a fielded pack that imports them still loads, and READ wherever an
101	// outcome is decoded: labels are stored data on closed issues fleet-wide, so a
102	// decoder that stopped recognising these would turn every historical run into an
103	// un-outcomed one. Write `TASK_DONE` / `TASK_OBSOLETE`.
104	export const OUTCOME_DONE = 'outcome:done';
105	export const OUTCOME_OBSOLETE = 'outcome:obsolete';
106	
107	// Today's terminal spellings (DESIGN §4, §15.25): the `outcome:` namespace dissolves
108	// into `task:`, one vocabulary for the state machine's live and terminal states
109	// alike. These are what the engine WRITES; the `outcome:*` spellings above are read
110	// forever, because a closed issue keeps whatever it was closed under.
111	export const TASK_DONE = 'task:done';
112	export const TASK_OBSOLETE = 'task:obsolete';
113	
114	// The stored-data rename rule, decode side: every spelling ever written maps
115	// STRAIGHT to the canonical word, in one pass — including `outcome:delivered`,
116	// which nothing writes any more but closed issues carry forever.
117	const OUTCOME_SPELLINGS = new Map([
118	  [TASK_DONE, 'done'], [OUTCOME_DONE, 'done'],
119	  [OUTCOME_DELIVERED, 'delivered'],
120	  [TASK_OBSOLETE, 'obsolete'], [OUTCOME_OBSOLETE, 'obsolete'],
121	]);
122	
123	// The one outcome an issue's labels carry, as the canonical word ('done',
124	// 'delivered', 'obsolete') or null. Everything that tallies or renders outcomes
125	// decodes through here, so a spelling change is one map entry and not a sweep.
126	export function outcomeOf(issue) {
127	  for (const l of labelNames(issue)) {
128	    const o = OUTCOME_SPELLINGS.get(l);
129	    if (o) return o;
130	  }
131	  return null;
132	}
133	
134	// --- the request vocabulary (DESIGN §16.1) ------------------------------------
135	// Five labels in their own namespace, worn by an ORDINARY issue somebody marked —
136	// never by a work item, which is why they are not in the `task:` namespace and why
137	// nothing here reads them off an item. They are here beside the item's own
138	// vocabulary because they are the other half of the same compatibility surface.
139	//
140	// The mark is a LABEL rather than a body syntax or a command comment for one
141	// reason: it must be appliable from the issue page on a phone. It is also
142	// write-gated by the platform — applying a label needs triage or write access —
143	// which is the first half of the security story (the second is the precondition's
144	// permission read at pickup, §16.4).
145	export const REQUEST_LABEL = 'claude-task';
146	export const QUEUED_LABEL = 'claude-queued';
147	export const IN_REVIEW_LABEL = 'claude-in-review';
148	export const MODEL_LABEL_PREFIX = 'claude-model:';
149	
150	// The merge authorization (§16.11): the asker says up front that this request's
151	// change may land without their approval WHEN ITS DIFF IS NARROW — the run still
152	// judges the diff, and a wide one parks for review exactly as an unauthorized
153	// request does. Consumed with the mark like the model labels, so each ask
154	// authorizes afresh and a label left by an earlier ask never carries into a new one.
155	export const AUTOMERGE_LABEL = 'claude-automerge';
156	
157	// The families a request may ask for, and the one it gets when it asks for
158	// nothing. `none` is not among them: a request is implemented by a session, so an
159	// agentless family would name a run that cannot happen.
160	export const REQUEST_MODELS = Object.freeze(['opus', 'sonnet', 'haiku']);
161	export const DEFAULT_REQUEST_MODEL = 'opus';
162	
163	export const MODEL_LABELS = REQUEST_MODELS.map((f) => `${MODEL_LABEL_PREFIX}${f}`);
164	
165	// Every label the request mode applies, ensured like the queue's own. `claude-task`
166	// is ensured too although only a person applies it: a label that does not exist is
167	// one nobody can find in the picker, and the mark is the whole entry point.
168	export const REQUEST_LABELS = [
169	  { name: REQUEST_LABEL, color: '1d76db', description: 'Claudinite: implement this issue — the next scheduler run queues a run for it' },
170	  { name: QUEUED_LABEL, color: 'fbca04', description: 'Claudinite: a work item exists for this issue' },
171	  { name: IN_REVIEW_LABEL, color: '5319e7', description: 'Claudinite: a pull request is open for this issue, waiting on a person' },
172	  { name: AUTOMERGE_LABEL, color: '0e8a16', description: 'Claudinite: land this request without approval if its diff is narrow (docs, tests, comments, code in one directory)' },
173	  ...REQUEST_MODELS.map((f) => ({
174	    name: `${MODEL_LABEL_PREFIX}${f}`, color: 'ededed',
175	    description: `Claudinite: run this request at the ${f} family`,
176	  })),
177	];
178	
179	// The model a marked issue asks for, from the labels standing on it. An
180	// unrecognised family falls back to the default rather than failing the request:
181	// a run nobody can start would look accepted forever. Where several are present the
182	// order is REQUEST_MODELS' — the labels are consumed at adoption (§16.3), so the
183	// only way to hold two is to apply two for the same ask.
184	export const requestModelFromLabels = (labels = []) => {
185	  const asked = labels.filter((l) => l.startsWith(MODEL_LABEL_PREFIX)).map((l) => l.slice(MODEL_LABEL_PREFIX.length));
186	  return REQUEST_MODELS.find((f) => asked.includes(f)) ?? DEFAULT_REQUEST_MODEL;
187	};
188	
189	// The four state labels an open item may wear. An open item wearing none of them
190	// and no `needs-human` is off the state machine entirely — a torn label swap's
191	// leavings, which the janitor repairs (DESIGN §6.2, §11).
192	export const STATE_LABELS = [BLOCKED, READY, EXECUTING, AGENT];
193	
194	// Every label this mechanism applies, with the colour and description a bootstrap
195	// one-off would have given it. Ensured create-if-missing before anything is
196	// applied: GitHub 422s when you apply an unknown label and never creates one on
197	// demand, so the thing that assigns a label guarantees it first.
198	export const QUEUE_LABELS = [
199	  { name: BLOCKED, color: 'c5def5', description: 'Claudinite queue: waiting on Blocked-by and/or Not-before' },
200	  { name: READY, color: '0e8a16', description: 'Claudinite queue: available for an executor to pick up' },
201	  { name: URGENT, color: 'd93f0b', description: 'Claudinite queue: pick this before any non-urgent item' },
202	  { name: EXECUTING, color: 'fbca04', description: 'Claudinite queue: an executor holds the claim' },
203	  { name: AGENT, color: '1d76db', description: 'Claudinite queue: an agent session owns this item' },
204	  { name: NEEDS_HUMAN, color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite queue: parked for a human — the one triage state' },
205	  { name: NEEDS_HUMAN_ACTION, color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite triage: a human must change something outside the code' },
206	  { name: NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION, color: 'd93f0b', description: 'Claudinite triage: a human must choose what happens next' },
207	  { name: NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL, color: '5319e7', description: 'Claudinite triage: succeeded and left an unmerged PR to approve' },
208	  { name: NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE, color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite triage: the run broke — diagnose and fix' },
209	  { name: TASK_DONE, color: '0e8a16', description: 'Claudinite queue: succeeded, nothing pending' },
210	  { name: OUTCOME_DELIVERED, color: '5319e7', description: 'Claudinite queue: succeeded and left a live artifact the world still has to act on' },
211	  { name: TASK_OBSOLETE, color: 'ededed', description: 'Claudinite queue: never ran — the precondition said no, or the task is gone' },
212	];
213	
214	// GitHub hands labels back as objects on the issues API and as bare strings in
215	// some fixtures; accept either.
216	export const labelNames = (issue) =>
217	  (issue?.labels ?? []).map((l) => (typeof l === 'string' ? l : l?.name)).filter(Boolean);
218	
219	export const hasLabel = (issue, name) => labelNames(issue).includes(name);
220	
221	// Title. The optional qualifier exists ONLY for deliberately concurrent items —
222	// a fan-out naming its target — and it is part of the identity the same-title
223	// mutex reads (DESIGN §6.1). Nothing ever encodes a date here: that was the slot
224	// grammar, and the issue number is the identity (DESIGN §5).
225	export const workItemTitle = ({ pack, task, qualifier = null }) =>
226	  `${WORK_PREFIX} ${pack}/${task}${qualifier ? ` ${qualifier}` : ''}`;
227	
228	// pack and task ids are single path segments; the qualifier is whatever follows.
229	const TITLE_RE = /^\[claudinite-work\]\s+([^/\s]+)\/([^/\s]+)(?:\s+(\S.*))?$/;
230	
231	// The pack half is canonicalized on the way out. A work item's title is STORED
232	// DATA — it sits on an open GitHub issue that outlives any one converge — so items
233	// filed before a pack was renamed still carry the old spelling. Read literally, the
234	// scheduler run would not recognise its own live item, would file a second one beside it, and
235	// would leave the first orphaned in the queue with nothing ever draining it.
236	export function parseWorkItemTitle(title) {
237	  const m = TITLE_RE.exec(String(title ?? '').trim());
238	  return m ? { pack: canonicalPackId(m[1]), task: m[2], qualifier: m[3]?.trim() || null } : null;
239	}
240	
241	export const isWorkItemTitle = (title) => parseWorkItemTitle(title) !== null;
242	
243	// STANDING OR AD-HOC, DERIVED (DESIGN §15.26). A task's standing item is the one
244	// the generator files at an anchor: its title names the task and nothing else, and
245	// the task it names is on a calendar. Everything else is ad-hoc — a `manual` task
246	// (which has no anchor to stand for) and every qualified item (a fan-out target, a
247	// request naming its issue), each of which may legitimately run beside the
248	// occurrence rather than being it.
249	//
250	// It is read off the item and the declaration at HEAD rather than off a label the
251	// creator applied, because the two could disagree: a marker says what its writer
252	// believed, the structure says what the item IS, and the guards that consume this
253	// (the occurrence guard, the dedupe, the `after` yield) are only sound on the
254	// second. `frequency` is the declared frequency of the task the title names —
255	// absent when the repo no longer carries it, which is ad-hoc by the same rule.
256	export function isStandingItem(item, frequency) {
257	  const parsed = parseWorkItemTitle(item?.title ?? item);
258	  return !!parsed && parsed.qualifier === null && frequency != null && frequency !== 'manual';
259	}
260	
261	// --- comment markers ----------------------------------------------------------
262	// The three comments the protocol reads back. They are HTML comments so a human
263	// reading the item sees prose, and they are here — with the labels and the body
264	// fields — because together they ARE the item's vocabulary, the one compatibility
265	// surface across engine versions (DESIGN §14).
266	//
267	// The CLAIM comment carries who and when (executor identity is an unbounded set
268	// and must never become a label). The HANDOFF comment names the session and the
269	// invocation nonce. The EPISODE comment is the boundary the claim arbiter is
270	// scoped to: every claim before it is dead, and arbitrating over dead claims makes
271	// one outrank every future live claimant — the item then livelocks through reclaim
272	// cycles forever (F18). A reclaim, a revert and a hand re-queue each write one.
273	export const CLAIM_MARKER = '<!-- claudinite-claim -->';
274	export const HANDOFF_MARKER = '<!-- claudinite-handoff -->';
275	export const EPISODE_MARKER = '<!-- claudinite-episode -->';
276	
277	// --- the body -----------------------------------------------------------------
278	
279	export const NOT_BEFORE_FIELD = 'Not-before';
280	export const BLOCKED_BY_FIELD = 'Blocked-by';
281	
282	// The three fields a REQUEST item carries (DESIGN §16.3, §16.11). `Request` is the issue this
283	// run implements — the whole payload, since the request task has no code-work phase
284	// to hand one over. `Model` is the family the asker chose, copied here by the scheduler run
285	// from a write-gated label and read only by a task that declares
286	// `model_from_request`; it is the first thing an item carries that defines
287	// behaviour, which is why it is fenced rather than waved through (§16.7).
288	export const REQUEST_FIELD = 'Request';
289	export const MODEL_FIELD = 'Model';
290	
291	// `Merge` is the asker's standing authorization, copied here from the
292	// write-gated `claude-automerge` label. Its one value is `if-narrow`: the run may
293	// land its own pull request when the diff classifier calls the diff narrow, and
294	// must park for approval otherwise. An absent field is the default — never merge —
295	// so an item an older scheduler run wrote reads as unauthorized rather than as authorized.
296	export const MERGE_FIELD = 'Merge';
297	export const MERGE_IF_NARROW = 'if-narrow';
298	
299	// The heading the delivered-artifacts section carries in a work item body. One
300	// home, because it is written in three places and MATCHED when a re-entrant run
301	// updates the section it already wrote.
302	export const DELIVERED_HEADING = 'Delivered by code-work';
303	
304	// The same heading as earlier renames spelled it. A live item's body still carries
305	// whichever word was current when its section was first written, and matching only
306	// today's would append a SECOND section rather than updating that one.
307	export const LEGACY_DELIVERED_HEADINGS = Object.freeze([
308	  'Delivered by prework',
309	  'Delivered by code_work',
310	]);
311	
312	const NOT_BEFORE_RE = /^Not-before:[ \t]*(.*)$/m;
313	const BLOCKED_BY_RE = /^Blocked-by:[ \t]*(.*)$/m;
314	const REQUEST_RE = /^Request:[ \t]*#?(\d+)/m;
315	const MODEL_RE = /^Model:[ \t]*(\S+)/m;
316	const MERGE_RE = /^Merge:[ \t]*(\S+)/m;
317	
318	// Build a work item body. The first line is the task path — the only thing an
319	// executor reads to locate the worker, validated in code before anything trusts
320	// it. Everything behavior-defining (model, ceiling, worker content, code-work
321	// command) is read from the tracked task files at HEAD, never from here.
322	export function workItemBody({
323	  taskPath, notBefore = null, blockedBy = [], context = [], delivered = [], reason = null,
324	  request = null, model = null, merge = null,
325	}) {
326	  const lines = [taskPath, ''];
327	  const fields = [];
328	  if (notBefore) fields.push(`${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${notBefore}`);
329	  if (blockedBy.length) fields.push(`${BLOCKED_BY_FIELD}: ${blockedBy.map((n) => `#${n}`).join(', ')}`);
330	  if (request) fields.push(`${REQUEST_FIELD}: #${request}`);
331	  if (model) fields.push(`${MODEL_FIELD}: ${model}`);
332	  if (merge) fields.push(`${MERGE_FIELD}: ${merge}`);
333	  if (fields.length) lines.push(...fields, '');
334	  lines.push('Execute the Claudinite task above.');
335	  if (context.length) {
336	    lines.push(
337	      'The Context section below is binding scope — do not re-decide it.',
338	      '',
339	      '### Context',
340	      ...context.map((c) => `- ${c}`),
341	    );
342	  }
343	  if (reason) lines.push('', '### Why the agent is here', '', `- ${reason}`);
344	  if (delivered.length) lines.push('', `### ${DELIVERED_HEADING}`, '', ...delivered.map((d) => `- ${d}`));
345	  return lines.join('\n') + '\n';
346	}
347	
348	// The `Blocked-by` numbers a body names, from a work item's body or from an
349	// ORDINARY issue's — a request marked for implementation states what it waits on in
350	// the same field spelling, and adoption carries it onto the item it births (§16.11).
351	export function parseBlockedBy(body) {
352	  const bb = BLOCKED_BY_RE.exec(String(body ?? ''))?.[1] ?? '';
353	  return [...bb.matchAll(/#(\d+)/g)].map((m) => Number(m[1]));
354	}
355	
356	// Parse an item body back into the facts the scheduler run and the executor read. A body
357	// with no first line, or whose fields are absent, yields nulls — absence is
358	// meaningful everywhere here and is never filled in with a default.
359	export function parseWorkItemBody(body) {
360	  const text = String(body ?? '');
361	  const taskPath = text.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).find((l) => l !== '') ?? null;
362	  const nb = NOT_BEFORE_RE.exec(text)?.[1]?.trim() || null;
363	  const blockedBy = parseBlockedBy(text);
364	  const request = REQUEST_RE.exec(text) ? Number(REQUEST_RE.exec(text)[1]) : null;
365	  // An unrecognised family reads as absent rather than as itself: the item's model
366	  // is behaviour-defining, so the only values that leave this parser are ones the
367	  // engine can actually dispatch at (§16.7).
368	  const askedModel = MODEL_RE.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
369	  const model = REQUEST_MODELS.includes(askedModel) ? askedModel : null;
370	  // Same fencing as the model: an unrecognised authorization reads as absent, and
371	  // absent is the safe end of this field — a run that cannot read its permission
372	  // opens a pull request and waits.
373	  const askedMerge = MERGE_RE.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
374	  const merge = askedMerge === MERGE_IF_NARROW ? askedMerge : null;
375	  return { taskPath, notBefore: nb, blockedBy, request, model, merge };
376	}
377	
378	// The item's own `### Context` bullets, in order — the binding scope a hand-created
379	// item was born with. Read back rather than kept only for the agent to read,
380	// because an operator's PARAMETERS ride here: `create-work-item --context
381	// "REPOS=Alpha Beta"` is how a forced run says what it is running on, and the
382	// executor hands these lines to code-work as `CLAUDINITE_CONTEXT`.
383	//
384	// A section runs to the next `### ` heading or to the end of the body — the same
385	// bounds `withSection` writes to — and only `- ` bullets count, so the prose
386	// framing around a section contributes nothing.
387	function sectionLines(body, heading) {
388	  const lines = String(body ?? '').split('\n');
389	  const at = lines.findIndex((l) => l.trim() === `### ${heading}`);
390	  if (at === -1) return [];
391	  const out = [];
392	  for (const line of lines.slice(at + 1)) {
393	    if (line.startsWith('### ')) break;
394	    const m = /^-[ \t]+(.*)$/.exec(line);
395	    if (m) out.push(m[1].trim());
396	  }
397	  return out;
398	}
399	
400	export const parseContextLines = (body) => sectionLines(body, 'Context');
401	
402	// --- the roll's record ----------------------------------------------------------
403	
404	// The section a no-go roll keeps on the item: the last declined reason and the next
405	// wake, REPLACED on every roll (the item is a status line, not a log — the timeline
406	// carries the history). Serializer and parser live together so the shape has one
407	// home; the executor writes it, and anything answering "why didn't it run" — the
408	// dashboard above all — reads it back.
409	export const LAST_VERDICT_HEADING = 'Last verdict';
410	
411	export function lastVerdictLines({ at, reason, until }) {
412	  const lines = [`${at} — the precondition declined: ${reason}`];
413	  if (until) lines.push(`Asked again at ${until}.`);
414	  return lines;
415	}
416	
417	export function parseLastVerdict(body) {
418	  const lines = sectionLines(body, LAST_VERDICT_HEADING);
419	  // The reason may carry the separator itself, so the split is on the FIRST match.
420	  const first = /^(.*?) — the precondition declined: ([\s\S]*)$/.exec(lines[0] ?? '');
421	  if (!first) return null;
422	  const until = lines.map((l) => /^Asked again at (.*?)\.?$/.exec(l)).find(Boolean)?.[1] ?? null;
423	  return { at: first[1], reason: first[2], until };
424	}
425	
426	// Fold a second set of Context lines into the first, keeping order and dropping
427	// exact duplicates. Both sides are real scope — the item carries what its creator
428	// bound it to, the precondition adds what this occurrence found — and a set-write
429	// from either side would drop the other's.
430	export const mergeContext = (...groups) => [...new Set(groups.flat().filter((l) => l && l.trim()))];
431	
432	// Stamp (or clear) `Not-before` on an existing body, in place where the field is
433	// already present and directly under the task path otherwise. Text surgery rather
434	// than a rebuild: the body also carries the creating precondition's Context and
435	// code-work's Delivered section, which belong to whoever wrote them.
436	export function withNotBefore(body, iso) {
437	  const text = String(body ?? '');
438	  if (NOT_BEFORE_RE.test(text)) {
439	    return iso
440	      ? text.replace(NOT_BEFORE_RE, `${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${iso}`)
441	      : text.replace(/^Not-before:[ \t]*.*\n?/m, '');
442	  }
443	  if (!iso) return text;
444	  const lines = text.split('\n');
445	  const at = lines.findIndex((l) => l.trim() !== '');
446	  if (at === -1) return `${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${iso}\n`;
447	  lines.splice(at + 1, 0, '', `${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${iso}`);
448	  return lines.join('\n');
449	}
450	
451	// Set a section of an item body (the Context, code-work's Delivered, the agent's Why)
452	// — replacing one of the same heading if it is already there, appending otherwise.
453	//
454	// REPLACING IS THE WHOLE POINT, and appending was a live bug (#879). Every standing
455	// item is born carrying a `### Context`, and the hand-off writes Context again — so
456	// an append leaves TWO sections of that name, while the session is told to read "the
457	// issue's Context section", singular. The one it reads first is then the scheduler run's birth
458	// note and the binding scope is in the other, which fails silently whichever section
459	// the agent picks. It also grows: an item re-queued through hand-off twice carried a
460	// third.
461	//
462	// A section runs to the next `### ` heading or to the end of the body, so a replaced
463	// section keeps its position rather than migrating to the bottom — the body stays in
464	// the order a reader learned it.
465	// `aliases` are older spellings of the SAME heading. The section is rewritten under
466	// `heading`, but located by any of them, so a body written before a rename is updated
467	// in place instead of gaining a second section.
468	export function withSection(body, heading, lines, aliases = []) {
469	  if (!lines.length) return body;
470	  const text = String(body ?? '').replace(/\s*$/, '');
471	  const section = [`### ${heading}`, '', ...lines.map((l) => `- ${l}`)];
472	  const existing = text.split('\n');
473	  const wanted = new Set([heading, ...aliases].map((h) => `### ${h}`));
474	  const at = existing.findIndex((l) => wanted.has(l.trim()));
475	  if (at === -1) return `${text}\n\n${section.join('\n')}\n`;
476	  const after = existing.findIndex((l, i) => i > at && l.startsWith('### '));
477	  const tail = after === -1 ? [] : ['', ...existing.slice(after)];
478	  return `${[...existing.slice(0, at), ...section, ...tail].join('\n')}\n`;
479	}

1	# Task dispatch without slots — the work-item queue
2	
3	The mechanism lives in [`engine/scheduler/queue/`](../../engine/scheduler/queue/),
4	behind `taskScheduler.dispatch`. A continuation of the owner's sketch (2026-08-12, reproduced in Appendix A), played against twenty timed
5	scenarios ([SCENARIOS.md](SCENARIOS.md)) and the field's prior art
6	([RESEARCH.md](RESEARCH.md)), with the owner's eight decisions of 2026-08-13
7	recorded in §15 and folded into the sections they changed. The phase plan
8	belongs to a tracking issue, not here. It supersedes
9	the slot machinery of
10	[per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3–§5](../per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md) and
11	amends several of its §12 decisions (each amendment is named where it happens).
12	What it does **not** touch: the task folder anatomy (§1), the precondition
13	contract, code-work and its secrets model
14	([task-code-work DESIGN](../task-code-work/DESIGN.md)), the outcome ceiling, the
15	security posture (the issue is data; behavior comes from tracked files), and the
16	usage-metrics records.
17	
18	The shape in one paragraph: **work items are issues, available for work; any
19	number of executors pull from them.** A thin generator — one scheduler run on the repo's one cron — gives every
20	recurring task a standing work item at its anchor and flips blocked items
21	ready — pure label mechanics, no preconditions, no signals. An executor — a
22	GitHub Action by default, but anything that can read issues — picks up the
23	next ready item, claims it by label, evaluates the precondition (the only
24	place it ever runs): on a go it runs the work step and hands off to agentic work (a
25	CCR session invoked by API); on a no-go the item **rolls** — stamped
26	not-before the task's next anchor, blocked, reason recorded — so the item
27	itself carries "asked, declined, wakes at T". Follow-ups, fan-outs, urgency,
28	and one-off forcing are all just *creating or waking work items*. There is no
29	slot id, no run-ledger watermark, no exclusive claim, and no label-event
30	re-arm.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 1. What the slot machinery costs today
35	
36	The current design is push-shaped: one hourly scheduler run decides, at a single
37	instant, everything that will happen — which tasks are due, whether they run,
38	what they may touch — and encodes the decision into dispatch issues that a
39	label-event-triggered session then executes. Every complication below is a
40	consequence of that shape.
41	
42	- **The slot id is state smuggled into a title token.** `d2026-08-12`,
43	  `h2026-08-12T14Z`, `m2026-08` exist so that a scheduled occurrence has an
44	  identity — which the exactly-once guard needs (title search per slot), the
45	  stale backstop needs (the *leading character* of the slot id is parsed back
46	  into a period, `SLOT_PERIOD_MS`), and forcing needs (the `~f<runId>` marker
47	  appended so an operator re-run of an already-run slot isn't silently
48	  swallowed). Three mechanisms each decode a fragment of scheduler state out of
49	  a string in an issue title.
50	
51	- **Due-ness lives in a platform side channel.** "Has this slot run?" is
52	  answered by the Actions run ledger of the scheduler workflow itself
53	  (`lastSuccessTime`) — a watermark that is not visible beside the work, must
54	  exclude forced runs to stay correct, and whose unreadability has to fail the
55	  whole run (an exit-0 abort would advance it past slots it never evaluated).
56	  The state the system actually cares about — *was this occurrence's work
57	  created?* — is derivable from the issues themselves, and nothing reads it
58	  from there. *(A first cut of the go/no-go ruling briefly reintroduced a
59	  ledger read; the standing-item model (§5) removed it again — the scheduler run is
60	  now a pure function of the clock and the issue list.)*
61	
62	- **A decision made at one instant cannot express ordering, only simultaneity.**
63	  The nightly chain's ordering is faked by anchor-hour staggering, which
64	  collapses whenever GitHub fires the cron late — hence the `exclusive: true`
65	  claim, a task-level hack whose cost is real: **a deferred slot is spent, not
66	  queued**, so a claim on the wrong night silently halves throughput. The
67	  system has no way to say "run B after A"; it can only say "run A alone".
68	
69	- **Label-event invocation is lossy, and the loss shaped three mechanisms.**
70	  The executor routine fires only on a fresh `labeled` event; a lost delivery
71	  leaves an armed issue sitting forever. So: the janitor's re-arm
72	  (remove/re-add the label to emit a new event), the 20-minute grace window so
73	  a re-arm never hands a live session a rival, and the stale escalation that
74	  bounds the re-arm loop. The claim protocol then has to survive *duplicate*
75	  events (the read-swap-confirm lease). All of it is compensation for a trigger
76	  that neither confirms delivery nor can be polled.
77	
78	- **Capacity, urgency, and follow-ups have no home.** There is exactly one
79	  implicit executor per repo and no way to add another; nothing distinguishes
80	  urgent work from routine work; a task cannot schedule a successor ("validate
81	  in two days what tonight's run delivered") except by hoping a future
82	  precondition rediscovers the situation. Forcing (`FORCE_TASKS`) is a special
83	  engine path with its own exemptions (skips preconditions, exempt from
84	  deferral, excluded from the watermark, slot-id marker) — where "run this now"
85	  ought to be the system's most ordinary operation.
86	
87	- **Visibility is split three ways.** Whether something *will* run is ledger
88	  math nobody can see; whether it *is* running is labels on an issue; what it
89	  *did* is a record line in a captured transcript. There is no one place where
90	  the state of the repo's recurring work can be read.
91	
92	What is worth keeping — and this design keeps all of it — is everything the
93	incidents taught: one session executes exactly one item and never sweeps the
94	queue (the duplicate-execution bug, DESIGN §5), the claim is a verified lease,
95	the issue is data and never instructions, behavior-defining content comes only
96	from tracked files, every exit converges to one visible terminal state, and
97	recovery lives in one place, in code.
98	
99	## 2. The shape — a pull-based queue of work items
100	
101	Four roles, strictly separated (this refines, rather than replaces, the
102	2026-08-06 three-responsibility split — the scheduler's job splits in two and
103	shrinks):
104	
105	1. **The generator** — a thin scheduled run (the repo's one cron, unchanged
106	   rule). Three jobs, all deterministic label mechanics over the issue list:
107	   *instantiate* each recurring task's standing item when its time comes,
108	   *ready* blocked items whose dependencies have resolved and whose not-before
109	   has passed, and *reclaim* dead executor claims. It evaluates no
110	   preconditions and collects no signals (§5); it executes nothing.
111	2. **Executors** — any number of pull workers. Each iteration: pick the next
112	   ready item (urgent first), claim it, evaluate the precondition — the only
113	   place it is ever evaluated — then on a go run the work step and either finish
114	   (agentless task) or invoke the agentic phase and hand the item to it; on a
115	   no-go, roll a scheduled item to its next anchor (§5). An executor is
116	   platform-agnostic by construction: its whole interface is issue read/write
117	   plus the repo at HEAD. More capacity = more executors.
118	3. **Agents** — CCR sessions, one per handed-off item, invoked by the executor.
119	   An agent executes its one item's task file, verifies its outcome ceiling,
120	   and converges the item to a terminal state.
121	4. **The janitor** — unchanged in role, smaller in scope: dead executor claims,
122	   dead agent claims, stale-item escalation, queue health review. The re-arm
123	   retires (§11).
124	
125	The queue itself is the repo's issues, and under the standing-item model that
126	sentence is complete: everything the system knows — including "this task was
127	asked, declined, and wakes again at T" — is on a work item. No plan file, no
128	watermark, no ledger read. The scheduler run is a pure function of the clock and the
129	issue list; which is what the sketch means by *visibility into state*.
130	
131	## 3. The work item
132	
133	An issue, `[claudinite-work] <pack>/<task>` (plus an optional free-form
134	qualifier after the task, for tasks that legitimately have several concurrent
135	items — a fan-out names its target: `[claudinite-work] sheepdog/fleet-baseline
136	member-repo-x`). **The issue number is the identity.** No slot id: an
137	occurrence needs no name beyond the item that embodies it, and everything the
138	slot id encoded is recovered elsewhere — dedup from the family's creation
139	timestamps (§5), staleness from the task's own declared frequency read at HEAD
140	(§11), forcing from the fact that creating an item *is* forcing (§8).
141	
142	Body, machine-first (same parsing discipline as today's dispatch body — the
143	first line is the task path, validated in code before anything trusts it):
144	
145	```
146	.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/baselining/task.md
147	
148	Not-before: 2026-08-14T04:00Z            # optional — see §9
149	Blocked-by: #812, #813                   # optional — see §9
150	
151	Execute the Claudinite task above.
152	The Context section below is binding scope — do not re-decide it.
153	
154	### Context
155	- <the creating precondition's binding lines, verbatim — unchanged>
156	
157	### Delivered by code-work
158	- <written by the executor at hand-off, unchanged shape>
159	```
160	
161	Everything behavior-defining — model, outcome ceiling, worker content, the
162	work step's command — is still read from the tracked task files at HEAD, never from the
163	issue. A work item whose task the repo no longer carries is closed as obsolete,
164	exactly like today's exit-14.
165	
166	**Standing vs ad-hoc is structural — there is no origin marker** (owner,
167	2026-08-19; this deletes `origin:schedule`, and `origin:request` dies unbuilt).
168	An **unqualified** item of a task with a frequency *is* that task's standing
169	item: the guards (§5) key on the bare title and the frequency read at HEAD, so
170	nothing is hand-classified. Everything else is ad-hoc — an item of a `manual`
171	task, or any item carrying a qualifier — and sits outside the family by its
172	very title, so scheduled work and ad-hoc work never suppress each other: a
173	pending follow-up (its own task) does not silence tomorrow's occurrence, and a
174	fan-out target (qualified) does not consume it. Two consequences, both
175	deliberate: creating an unqualified item of a scheduled task where none is
176	open **is** minting its standing item — the same act as §8's force lever, not
177	a lookalike — so deliberate concurrency for one task always names a qualifier;
178	and a request item needs no marker either, being known by its `Request:` field
179	(§16.3). The fielded engine still applies `origin:schedule` until the
180	vocabulary migration; the label becomes inert stored data the decoders ignore.
181	A task whose precondition should care about open follow-ups can see them
182	through the `issues` signal, as task-specific logic where it belongs.
183	
184	## 4. The state machine
185	
186	```
187	                     ┌────────────► closed  task:obsolete
188	                     │                    (precondition no longer holds; task gone)
189	 created ─► task:blocked ─► task:ready ─► task:executing ─► task:agent ─► closed  task:done
190	            (only when       (queue)       (claimed by an     (handed to        open    needs-human
191	             Blocked-by /                   executor)          a CCR session)           + one of the four
192	             Not-before                                                                   triage sub-labels
193	             present)
194	```
195	
196	Labels, the full vocabulary:
197	
198	| label | means | applied by |
199	|---|---|---|
200	| `task:blocked` | waiting on `Blocked-by` issues and/or `Not-before` | creator |
201	| `task:ready` | available for pickup | creator or the scheduler run |
202	| `task:urgent` | modifier: pick before any non-urgent item | creator (write-gated, like every label) |
203	| `task:executing` | an executor holds the claim | executor, on claim |
204	| `task:agent` | an agent session owns it | executor, at hand-off |
205	| `task:done` | succeeded; nothing pending (closed) | executor or agent |
206	| `outcome:delivered` | **retired 2026-08-19, still read.** Meant "succeeded and left a live artifact the world still has to act on"; an unmerged PR now parks at `task:needs-human-approval` instead of closing, and nothing else ever wrote it. Closed issues carrying it are stored data, so every decoder still recognises it | — (historical) |
207	| `task:obsolete` | never ran: the pickup-time precondition said no, or the task is gone from the repo (closed as not planned) | executor |
208	| `needs-human` | parked for a human — the one triage *state*, and what every guard, sweep and dashboard turns on (open) | anyone, incl. janitor |
209	| `task:needs-human-action` | …and something outside the code must change first: a secret set, a scope granted, a routine rewired, an input supplied | anyone, incl. janitor |
210	| `task:needs-human-decision` | …and the run stopped mid-flight, so the next step is a choice: re-queue or abandon, does the half-done work stand, was the ceiling violation acceptable | anyone, incl. janitor |
211	| `task:needs-human-approval` | …and it **succeeded**, deliberately leaving an unmerged PR. The one park that is not a fault | executor or agent |
212	| `task:needs-human-failure` | …and the run broke: a bug, a contract-forbidden shape, a malformed or forged item. The default when nothing else fits | anyone, incl. janitor |
213	
214	**The terminal labels live in the `task:` namespace** (owner, 2026-08-19):
215	`task:done` and `task:obsolete` — one vocabulary for the state machine's live
216	*and* terminal states, and the `outcome:` namespace dissolves. The fielded
217	engine writes the old spellings (`outcome:done`, `outcome:obsolete`) until the
218	vocabulary migration lands; per the stored-data rename rule, decoders map
219	every legacy spelling straight to today's, and `outcome:delivered` — which
220	nothing writes — stays a recognized legacy spelling forever.
221	
222	**Every park wears two labels**: `needs-human` *and* exactly one sub-label. The
223	state and the routing are different questions — the machine reads the first, a
224	person reads the second — and collapsing them would have meant a migration to
225	land rather than an additive write (the collapse is #1050's, once the fleet has
226	converged past the split).
227	
228	**A park wearing no sub-label reads as `failure`.** That is the compatibility
229	direction chosen deliberately: every item an engine older than the split left
230	behind, and every kind word a newer engine invents that this one does not know,
231	holds the lane rather than silently letting a broken task keep filing work.
232	
233	**Only a `failure` park holds the task's lane** (§5). An open unqualified item
234	of a scheduled task *is* its standing item (§3), so while one exists no further
235	occurrence is filed — for a break that is the point, since a queue of items that will fail the
236	same way helps nobody and the silence is the signal. For the other three it is a
237	bug: a PR waiting on a reviewer, a decision waiting on its owner and a secret
238	waiting to be set are one person's inbox, not a fault in the task, and #1032
239	measured what conflating them costs — a permission gap parked `missingbulb/Shepherd`'s
240	`fleet-digest` for two days while its dashboard read healthy, because no item was
241	ever filed behind the parked one. So the generator drops non-blocking parks from
242	both the standing-item test and the duplicate sweep beside it.
243	
244	This is the sketch's lifecycle with two adjustments, both argued for rather
245	than assumed:
246	
247	- **Executor identity is a claim comment, not a label.** The sketch's
248	  `being-handled-by-executor-1` puts an unbounded set (executor identities) into
249	  a vocabulary that must stay small and queryable; every new executor would mint
250	  a label, and a query for "what is executing" would have to know every
251	  executor's name. One state label (`task:executing`) answers the query; the
252	  claim comment — which the lease protocol requires anyway — carries *who*
253	  (executor id, run URL) and *when*. Same for `task:agent`: the hand-off
254	  comment names the CCR session.
255	- **`succeeded-with-unexpected-result` became `outcome:delivered`, and then
256	  became a park.** "Unexpected" would blur two things that must not blur: a run
257	  that legitimately left a pending artifact within its ceiling (open-pr task →
258	  open PR: *expected*, but the world hasn't finished with it), and a run that
259	  violated its ceiling (a `none` task that opened a PR). The second is still a
260	  **failure**, now `task:needs-human-decision` — someone must say whether the
261	  overreach stands — exactly as `verify-outcome` enforces. The first turned out
262	  not to be a terminal state at all: a PR nobody has merged is waiting on a
263	  named person, and closing the item hid that from every surface that counts
264	  open work, so it parks at `task:needs-human-approval` and stays open. It does
265	  not hold the lane, so the reviewer's silence delays only the review.
266	
267	Terminal-state discipline is unchanged: every item converges exactly once to
268	exactly one end — one of the two closes, or a park under one of the four
269	sub-labels — with one comment saying what happened.
270	
271	**Label writes are granular, always** ([RESEARCH](RESEARCH.md) §2): add and
272	remove named labels (REST POST/DELETE), never write the label *set* (PUT,
273	GraphQL `updateIssue`) — a set-write replaces from a stale snapshot and
274	clobbers concurrent transitions, a bug class GitHub's own CLI shipped
275	([cli/cli#4861](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/4861)). With multiple
276	executors and a scheduler run all moving labels, this is a correctness rule, not a
277	style preference.
278	
279	**The road back from `needs-human`** (SCENARIOS S12/S19, F7): a human who has
280	resolved the cause re-queues the item by removing `needs-human` and its
281	sub-label and applying `task:ready` — the sanctioned retry lever, write-gated like every label
282	operation here. The next pickup re-runs the precondition (§6.4), which is what
283	makes the retry safe even when the failed run half-did its work. Alternatively
284	the human closes the item (optionally superseding it with a forced retry,
285	§8); nothing mechanical ever re-queues a `needs-human` item.
286	
287	## 5. The generator — the standing work item
288	
289	> Amended 2026-08-18 (§16.3): the scheduler run has a **fourth** job, `adopt` — an ordinary
290	> issue marked `claude-task` becomes a work item, and the mark is consumed in the
291	> same pass. It is the same kind of job as the other three: label mechanics over
292	> the issue list, no precondition, no signal.
293	
294	**The scheduler run never evaluates a precondition and never collects a signal**
295	(owner model, 2026-08-13). Creation is calendar-only: at a task's anchor, the
296	scheduler run creates its work item *unconditionally* — the precondition speaks later,
297	at pickup, on the executor (§6.4), which is where the original sketch had it
298	all along. What happens on a no-go is the model's whole trick: the item is
299	**not closed** — the executor stamps it `Not-before: <the task's next anchor>`,
300	swaps it back to `task:blocked`, records the reason, and the item **rolls
301	forward**. The next anchor readies it again; the next pick re-asks. One ask
302	per period, exactly — go/no-go preserved — and the memory of "evaluated,
303	declined, ask again at T" is carried **on the item itself**, in the one place
304	this design keeps state.
305	
306	```text
307	scheduler run(now):
308	  if dormant: return                            # before any read, as today
309	
310	  # ---- job 1: instantiate (calendar-only; no preconditions, no signals) ----
311	  for task in discoverTasks():                  # NO ordering requirement — the
312	    if task.frequency == 'manual': continue     # `after` yield is pick-time (§6.1)
313	    A = mostRecentAnchor(task.frequency, config.taskScheduler, now)
314	    family = issues(title == "[claudinite-work] <pack>/<task>", state ALL)
315	                    # the exact bare title — a qualified item is outside the
316	                    # family structurally (§3), no marker involved
317	                    # REST issue list, never the search index (S6/F11)
318	    # A park that is somebody's INBOX rather than a fault does not hold the
319	    # lane: it is neither the standing item nor a duplicate of one, so it drops
320	    # out of the two OPEN tests below and the schedule goes on around it. A
321	    # `failure` park, and any park an older engine left unclassified, stays in
322	    # (§4). It stays in `family` for the occurrence guard further down, which is
323	    # the point: the parked item DID consume its own occurrence, so the next
324	    # item is filed at the next anchor and not immediately.
325	    live = [i for i in family if not (i has "needs-human" and not blockingPark(i))]
326	    # F16 self-heal first: nothing documents that a REST list from another
327	    # node sees a creation seconds old, so a stale list can let a duplicate
328	    # standing item through. Assume it will happen rather than that it won't:
329	    # close every open family item but the OLDEST, task:obsolete, with a
330	    # dedupe comment. Serialized by the scheduler run's concurrency group.
331	    if count(i.state == OPEN for i in live) > 1: closeAllButOldest(live)
332	    if any(i.state == OPEN for i in live):      continue  # the standing item
333	                                                          # already exists
334	    # the occurrence guard has TWO halves (F13, caught by the simulator): an
335	    # item CREATED at-or-after A covers this occurrence — and so does an item
336	    # CLOSED at-or-after A, because a rolled item created in an earlier
337	    # period that ran and closed today consumed today's occurrence. With the
338	    # created_at half alone, the very next scheduler run after such a close creates a
339	    # second item for the same occurrence: a double execution.
340	    if any(i.created_at >= A or i.closed_at >= A for i in family): continue
341	    createIssue(title:  "[claudinite-work] <pack>/<task>",
342	                body:   taskPath,
343	                labels: [family.isEmpty ? "task:blocked" : "task:ready"])
344	                # a brand-new task's FIRST item is born blocked with
345	                # Not-before = its next anchor — adoption must not fire
346	                # weekly/monthly tasks off-anchor (the old first-run concern)
347	
348	  # ---- job 2: ready whatever is due --------------------------------------
349	  for item in issues(label "task:blocked", state OPEN):   # any origin
350	    {blockedBy, notBefore} = parseBody(item)
351	    if all(issues(blockedBy).state == CLOSED) and now >= notBefore:
352	      swapLabel(item, "task:blocked" -> "task:ready")
353	
354	  # ---- job 3: reclaim dead executor claims (§11) --------------------------
355	  for item in issues(label "task:executing", state OPEN):
356	    if noActivitySince(item, EXECUTING_LEASH): stripToReady(item, comment)
357	```
358	
359	And the roll, executor-side (the full pick flow is §6):
360	
361	```text
362	on pick, verdict = precondition(signals, config):
363	  go     -> proceed (work step, hand-off, converge, CLOSE with an outcome)
364	  no-go  -> item is the task's standing item (§3 — unqualified, frequency at HEAD)?
365	              yes: Not-before = nextAnchor(task.frequency); ready -> blocked;
366	                   record the reason            # the item ROLLS — not an exit
367	              no:  close task:obsolete          # ad-hoc (manual task, or
368	                                                # qualified): no anchor to roll to (S17)
369	```
370	
371	**What this dissolves, all at once:**
372	
373	- **The evaluate-once ledger.** No `lastSchedulerRun`, no Actions-ledger read, no
374	  grace fallback: "was this occurrence evaluated" is answered by the standing
375	  item's own `Not-before`. §1's side-channel complaint is fully satisfied
376	  again — the scheduler run is a pure function of the clock and the issue list.
377	- **The 24-attempts cost (F10).** The scheduler run evaluates nothing; the precondition
378	  runs once per wake, i.e. once per period per task. Signals are collected by
379	  the executor for the one picked task — the scheduler run performs no GitHub reads
380	  beyond the issue list.
381	- **Declined occurrences were invisible in every earlier model** — no-go
382	  meant no item (or a ledger entry nobody sees). Now a quiet task's item shows
383	  its last ask, its reason, and its next wake, on its timeline. This closes
384	  the last gap in the sketch's *visibility into state*.
385	- **Forcing needs no item creation in the common case** (§8): the standing
386	  item exists, so force = wake it — strip `task:blocked`, clear `Not-before`,
387	  optionally add `task:urgent`. The same lever as the human re-queue (§4),
388	  which is no accident.
389	- **F9 (topological creation order) retires unbuilt**: `after` no longer
390	  wires `Blocked-by` at creation — see §6.1/§9 — so the scheduler run's iteration
391	  order stops mattering.
392	
393	**Titles carry no timestamp, and never will** (owner question, answered
394	plainly): every item of a task shares the bare title `[claudinite-work]
395	<pack>/<task>`; successive items are told apart by issue number, which is the
396	identity (§3). The optional qualifier exists only for deliberately concurrent
397	items (fan-out targets). Nothing ever parses a date out of a title — that was
398	the slot grammar, and it stays dead.
399	
400	**The costs, named:**
401	
402	- **The issue list's baseline changes meaning.** A quiet repo used to show
403	  zero open scheduler issues; now it shows one open (blocked) item per
404	  scheduled task, each stating its next wake. That is ~a dozen standing open
405	  issues here — read it as the dashboard it is: the issue list *is* the
406	  scheduler's state, which is what the sketch asked for. Filtering them out
407	  of "real issues" views is a title query — every work item wears the
408	  `[claudinite-work]` title prefix.
409	- **Hourly tasks churn their item.** An hourly task that stays no-go rolls
410	  ~24 times a day: two label flips and a body edit per roll, on one issue.
411	  Cheap against API quotas, noisy on that item's timeline; the roll writes no
412	  comment (the `Not-before` bump is the record) so the noise is timeline
413	  events, not comment spam. Named and accepted — one issue absorbs it.
414	- **A long-quiet task's item lives for months.** That is the feature wearing
415	  its cost: the item is the task's standing status line, and its age is
416	  information ("quiet since June"), not staleness — the janitor's stale rule
417	  keys on `task:ready` age, which a properly rolling item never accumulates.
418	
419	**Errored and forced items against the guards** (unchanged in substance from
420	the earlier draft, restated for the new shape):
421	
422	- A **failed run** parks its item open + `needs-human` (a real exit — the
423	  roll is only for no-go verdicts, never for failures). A `failure` park *is*
424	  the backlog guard: no new item until a human closes or re-queues it — one
425	  broken task, one triage item, however long it takes. The other three
426	  sub-labels are **not** guards (§4): a park that only wants a reviewer, a
427	  decision or a secret leaves the lane open, so the next occurrence is filed
428	  beside it on schedule. It still consumes its own occurrence, so nothing is
429	  filed until that next anchor.
430	- A **forced ad-hoc item** (qualified, or a manual task's — §3) is invisible
431	  to both guards in both directions, whatever state it ends in — its title is
432	  outside the family, so it neither suppresses nor consumes an occurrence
433	  (#749's property, now structural). An **unqualified** item of a scheduled
434	  task is never ad-hoc: creating one where none is open is minting the
435	  standing item (§8), and beside an open one it is a duplicate the F16
436	  self-heal closes.
437	- **Force-of-a-scheduled-task** is now the wake lever, not an item (§8), so
438	  the S15 same-title collision cannot arise from the common force at all; the
439	  pick mutex (§6.1) still covers a deliberately created concurrent item.
